interactions.title: Mos Numena worship and the Eight Divines
lines: DM: Yeah, so in, in Sembara it tends to be like each person has, like, a particular relationship. You know, there's somebody—some, one of the gods they tend to feel the closest to, for whatever reason. Like, that's... And, and they usually, um, would pray to that god to, like, intercede on their behalf with all the other gods.

DM: So, like, if your, if your personal deity is the Warlord and you need favor in a journey, which would be the domain of, um, The Wanderer, you would pray to the Warlord to ask for The Wanderer's favor.

DM: In Chardon, it's a bit less, um, centralized like that. There tends to be more kind of organized... You know, the temple of the, of The Wanderer has, like, the sort of, you know, The Wanderer's priesthood or whatever. That's a little bit more... It's, it's a little bit more centralized around...

DM: There's not the idea of, like, uh, like, the gods asking for favors on your behalf with each other. Um, it's a little bit more kind of, not exactly sects like most people would, but you would go to the temple of The Wanderer if you needed a favor of The Wanderer, that sort of thing.
Delwath: Mm. Um, but the vibe is always it's one religion-
Delwath: ... with eight sort of avatar divinities.
Delwath: It's not eight different gods who you...
DM: Yeah, you wouldn't call yourself a Wanderer-arian or something. You would always be, um-
Delwath: Like, you don't, nobody would be like, "Oh, yeah, I worship The Wanderer, but not The Mother."
Delwath: Like, it doesn't, they're not-
Unknown: Are there any, like, conflicts between these eight?
DM: They're, they, nobody really... I mean, they're all kind of archetypes, right? It's very much not like the Dunmari gods, which are seen as, like, kind of personal and almost humanized, right?
DM: Like, nobody really... Like, the, the gods don't even have names, right? Like, they're just The Wanderer or The Mother.
DM: Right? And everybody sort of-
Kenzo: But are they real the same way the Dunmari gods are real?

DM: Yeah, of course. Like, I mean, they literally saved humanity, right? There's plenty of miracles. Like, there's priests that cast spells from these. They're just not—they don't have that kind of personal vibe.
Delwath: They don't have personal st- It's not like they were... There's no vibe that they were, like-
DM: There's not, like, a story that they're-
Delwath: ... born or had a story, like, did stuff.
DM: ... there's not a story that they're siblings and they have, might have interpersonal rivalries.
Wellby: There's not even a sto- any story that they're a part of.
Wellby: ... they don't exist within a narrative whatsoever.
Delwath: Right. They don't, they don't do things.
Unknown: ... force or a way of being.
Delwath: They don't do things for themselves.
DM: They cause miracles. They don't, they don't have independent life apart.
Unknown: They, there's no s- myths of their independent life apart.

before: Kenzo: So if I need, like, a good harvest, I would go to this one or-
Seeker: Or, or is it more that there were sects that worshiped one in particular?
Delwath: But, but yeah, what's the-
DM: Well, I mean, in the modern day, it tends to be, um, at least in Chardon, where you're most familiar, um-
Delwath: But Wellby would know Sembara religion reasonably well, right?
after: Kenzo: When, when, when we do the, uh, the, the Downfall, um, uh, campaign, um, it'll be like, like, we'll be characters that end up becoming, like, the new kings, you know?
DM: [laughs]
Kenzo: 'Cause, like, there's no-
Delwath: Well, but they're already well established. They were already well established at Drankor during the Downfall.
Kenzo: Oh, well, anyways.

interactions.title: Yezali’s return and the lost gods
lines: DM: And the idea for—they're called in—incorporeal gods—is they are only created by the power of belief. So when you, when peop- so there are very likely... In fact, like, the, Delwath's whole backstory, right, is like that, Yezali, who was one of the, um-
DM: ... the Tanshi, which are these like small gods, was basically non-existent because-
Delwath: Was super weak 'cause Delwath was his only worshiper.
DM: ... the only person who knew about that, that god was just Delwath.
Delwath: That's why I had first level magic.
Unknown: Wait, why are you strong now?
Delwath: Well, because, uh, first of all, he found the other gods.
Delwath: He found the, a bunch of other Tanshi, and also I rescued Yezali from being trapped in the shadow dimension-
Delwath: ... in our little solo quest. That's what Delwath did, is he rescued Yezali and-
Delwath: ... reintroduced the culture, the Deno'qai, to Yezali.
DM: To the gods who they thought were dead.
Delwath: So, so now they know about him again.
Delwath: So they're like, "Oh, the god that we stopped worshiping-"
DM: ... they had, the Deno'qai had this term, the Meswati, the gods they thought were killed by Cha'mutte.
Delwath: But so now the gods have grown. I mean, they're still not that powerful.

before: Delwath: The elven gods came before the elves.
DM: Right.
Delwath: The human gods, on the other hand, came after the humans.
DM: Came after the humans.
Unknown: Right. Right, right, right.
after: Seeker: Wait, wait, this raises a kind of question whether we could do some—make a similar move on a much larger scale, which is to say, like reawaken the power of certain gods by encouraging like religious fervor among like vast populations of humans.

DM: So theoretically, although part of the, the deep lore is that for whatever as of yet unknown reason, something about Hkar made this kind of divine creation much, much easier. So lots of different gods were born-
Unknown: Oh.
Delwath: From the belief on Hkar.
DM: ... from the beliefs of people on Hkar, but new gods don't really seem to appear in the modern day very much.

lines: DM: Well, so there is... I mean, there's this, like, so for example, the Binding Stones, right? So there was, there were of course many different kinds of gods on-
Delwath: Yeah. Remember Sarqon, the god of slavery-

interactions.title: Ghesh gambles and describes the dragon’s rule
lines: DM: So you play, you play the first hand and, um, the, the, the biggest one, um-
Seeker: I have these two super dice, but no way to get it to Kenzo.
Kenzo: It's not a fight. I'm close.
DM: ... the sort of biggest one, he's, has the sort of most greenish tint on their back-
Kenzo: How far away are we?
DM: ... um, wins the, the first round and, and seems very happy and you're clo- close.
Kenzo: I, I toss him a Drankorian coin. I'm like-
DM: Yeah, so he wins a couple other coins.

DM: You don't know what you're doing, do ya?

Unknown: Okay, that's fine. That's fine.
Kenzo: Yeah, double or nothing. Let's go. [dice landing] I got you this time, Ghesh. Goddammit.
Kenzo: Kenzo like throws some like rocks. He's like...
DM: And he's like elbowing the other ones out of the way.
Kenzo: ... Kenzo throws a couple to this guy, Ghesh.
Delwath: You doing okay there, Kenzo?
Kenzo: Shut up, Delwath. Shut up, Delwath.
DM: I'm always happy to play dice with people who seemingly don't know the rules.
Delwath: Do you, do you need some help?
Kenzo: I mean, I know the rules, but you're just getting fucking lucky. It's fine.
DM: Oh, I'm not sure luck has anything to do with it.
Kenzo: This is a one-on-one game or is it like everybody like?
DM: Um, it's, it's kind of playing one-on... Like they're, they're kind of-
DM: ... trading off, right? So it's one-on-one.
DM: He's playing against the other-
Kenzo: So it's, there's three of them there?
DM: There's, uh, there's two of them there. There were four, but one flew up into the tower.
Kenzo: Right, right, right. Okay, so now... All right, so are any of the other ones wanting to play? Is, is, is, is it just, it's just been me and Ghesh one-on-one right now?

DM: It, the vibe that you get actually is that they, um, Ghesh is like the biggest and the bossiest of them, and seems to have, by some—maybe in that whispered conversation or by unspoken agreement—sort of muscled them out of the game. And as long as he's winning, isn't gonna let anybody else try and take his place.
Kenzo: What's the name of the guy that he mentioned? He said, he said, "Oh, somebody's gonna be happy."
Kenzo: Yeah. Yeah. Well, you don't get to keep these. You have to, you have to give them away to, uh, to Ra- what's the name? What's the other name you said?
Kenzo: Ra'ghemdros. You don't get to keep these?
DM: You don't bring coin on this island. Every single shiny thing belongs to her.
DM: Obviously. Wait, do you have more of these?
Kenzo: I mean, just a couple.
Unknown: Ask who r- who... Ask, ask Ra'ghemdros.
DM: What else are you car- you're...
DM: What else are you carrying? Maybe we should tell her about you.
Kenzo: Huh. Where does she live? Yeah, where does she live?
DM: Oh, there. She sort of—he points kind of—south-ish.
DM: In the burn scar, like potentially towards the burn scar maybe.
Kenzo: Potentially towards the burn scar.
Kenzo: You know, I saw that, that area that looked like all kind of red and a little destroyed. She lives in that place?
Kenzo: Or not destroyed, but you know.
DM: It's infused with her magic.
Kenzo: Huh. Wait and, and is she your friend?

DM: Um, friend? No, not so much friend. But she's gonna be my friend when I bring her this. There's like nothing, no coin left. There's nothing shiny left on the island for us to find, so sometimes she gets a bit grumpy.
Kenzo: Huh. But I mean, uh, d- does, is it... Do you guys have like a... Is... She's- she's your boss, huh? So like if you step out of line is she mean at all or is she...?
DM: Well, I mean, if you're hoarding coins, yeah, she'll kill you. But like, you know.
Kenzo: She's a dragon. She's a dragon.
DM: ... she's pretty easy to please.
Kenzo: She's pretty easy to please?
DM: You know, I- I- I heard a- a rumor from my friend Megren. She went to the mainland recently and came back with all sorts of great stuff, and now she's like got her own tower.
DM: So maybe he's eyeing you-
Kenzo: Was he saying his friend went to the mainland?
DM: Yes. His friend went to the mainland, Megren, brought back all sorts of stuff.
DM: And now Megren has her own tower.
Wellby: That's maybe a small coincidence but.
Delwath: Uh, did Megren perhaps take a piece of jade?
DM: And he's eyeing you kind of suspiciously, like trying to size you up. Like, how could he... could him and his friends jump you, and how much stuff do you have, and would he get his own tower?
DM: [laughs] Let's keep playing. I have a good feeling about this game.
Kenzo: I have a good feeling too. I've got a good feeling too. All right, let's do one more.
Wellby: If he wasn't there, couldn't they have all the towers?
Kenzo: That's a great question. [laughs] Kenzo laughs.
DM: The game is... He like shakes his fist. The game is done.
Kenzo: Oh, first I want to see some of yours. Give me one.
DM: He gives you like four of the stone tokens and does not give you back any of his coins.
Kenzo: [laughs] Kenzo pockets them, satisfied. That felt good.
Kenzo: So, so, so wait, so is, uh, uh, is your boss, um, they, they awake during the daytime? They sleeping? Can we meet them?
DM: Oh, you want to meet them? Oh yeah, that can be arranged.
DM: I think she'd be quite interested to talk to you if you're bringing the appropriate tribute. I mean, you got more of that?
Kenzo: Might be able to get some more. Is she, uh, uh... So wait, um, he's like a little reddish, reddish-
Kenzo: ... reddish-brown, huh? Is she red- reddish-brown like you?
DM: Oh, no, she's much scarier than me.
DM: Oh, she's like 10 times my size and black as shadow.
Kenzo: Black as shadow, huh? 10 times is not terrible.
Wellby: How, how long has she lived here?
Kenzo: Ask... Yeah, yeah. How long has she been here, and how long have you been here?
Kenzo: Forever. What does that mean forever, 1,000 years?
DM: [laughs] How would I know? I was only born 17 years ago.
Kenzo: You were only born 17 years ago?
Seeker: Huh. Ask if she likes to gamble.
Kenzo: Does she like to gamble?
DM: No. She just... Why would you gamble? She just takes your stuff. It's hers anyway.
DM: You brought it to the island, it's hers.
DM: You think you own your possessions? You don't.
Kenzo: ... have you guys had any other visitors-
DM: Not that I can remember.
Delwath: We should get an introduction to his friend who recently went to the mainland. Yeah. Ask if his friend likes to gamble.
Kenzo: Yeah. Does your friend like to gamble, that went to the mainland?
DM: Not anymore. She's got a tower. What does she need to gamble for?
Kenzo: Can we, can we meet them?
DM: Does she like to show off her tower?
Kenzo: Yeah. Could you tell us which one it is?
DM: He's kind of now annoyed that he lost and sort of is being a bit surly. Make a-
Kenzo: Kenzo, Kenzo, Kenzo throws another Drankorian coin his way.
DM: ... he smiles. He says, "Yeah, I'm sure she'd like to show off."
Kenzo: Yeah. Love to meet her.
Kenzo: Yeah, I'd love to see it.
DM: Well, there's a bad place in between. We have to go around.
Kenzo: What about this bad place?
DM: Um, you don't wanna go there. The statues are haunted by the spirits of the dead, and they'll kill you.
Kenzo: Hmm. Huh. Has, has it been this way for a long time?
DM: Sometimes you have bad dreams if you sleep too close.
Kenzo: Huh. How close are we now?
DM: It's like people choking and dying.
DM: I can take you though. Uh...
Kenzo: How far is it from here?
DM: Oh, you don't fly, do you?
Delwath: Little bit of a reveal there.
DM: It's not that far a walk, actually. It's just a little bit north... It's just a little bit west and then a little bit north.
DM: Maybe, like, uh, an hour.
Kenzo: All right. I'll follow you.
DM: You wanna go now? I mean, unless you're gonna lose some more.
DM: You got a few more of those coins?
Kenzo: You're killing me. Toss another one.
DM: I mean, you probably should be paying me a lot more 'cause-
Kenzo: How about a little bit now and then more when we get there, huh? Come on.

before: Kenzo: Wait, so-
Wellby: They can't lose.
Kenzo: Yeah.
Wellby: Now you're following Seeker's example.
Kenzo: [laughs] That's what I'm talking about.
after: Kenzo: Thank you.
Delwath: We should find out if one of them... So-
Kenzo: [laughs]
Delwath: That's good.
Kenzo: ... you're a lot taller than this little guy. You can kind of-

interactions.title: Promising a circlet for Ghesh’s silence
lines: Kenzo: Megren. Hey, and, uh, just, you know, between me and you... Toss a, toss like another couple coin. Um, I know your boss is interested in meeting us, meeting me. Meeting me, excuse me.

DM: Well, now it's a bargain. A few little coins isn't enough to buy my silence.
Kenzo: Yeah, sure. I toss him... I was like, I, I show him this one. You see this one?
Delwath: Do we have any gems?
Kenzo: You see, you see this one? Elves. Elven silver. Bet you haven't seen one of these before.
DM: I don't know. There was a lot here once, but it's all gone now. I mean, a lot less.
Kenzo: I know she's got it.
Kenzo: Yeah, but I mean, you know.
Delwath: No, no, no, let's give him something real, something that'll get him his own tower.
Kenzo: No, I'm just buying some silence right now. This is fine.
DM: He looks a little bit dubious.
DM: No, no, like just in general.

DM: He's just kind of standing there waiting.

Delwath: ... like, we could even, like, give him a story of where he f-
Delwath: Like that, why would he turn us in?
Kenzo: You like this one, huh?
DM: What, what did Kenzo want?
Delwath: We're, we're giving him a golden circlet with four-

DM: ... Grimbaskal. No, don't tell me. He's thinking for a minute, clearly making up a story. It came from a hidden ruin that we just discovered in the jungle. That's perfect.
Kenzo: Hidden ruin in the jungle. That's what's funny, that is where you found it.
DM: He's like clearly holding it in his hand.
Kenzo: I'm gonna give this to you after you introduce me to your friend.
Delwath: No, no, no. After he order—after the people who went up-
Delwath: ... have his whole clan come down here.
Delwath: So they don't fly off somewhere.
Delwath: When they're all standing around, you'll give it over.
Kenzo: Okay. I just want—I just need to make sure that you're not gonna tell, uh, tell your boss.

DM: He like whistles, and like eight of them come down, and he like turns and says, "Give me a minute." And he turns, and he like gives this speech in Draconic, which of course you can understand. He's like, "Look, guys, we've got an opportunity here." [laughs]
DM: And soon we'll have better digs, and we won't-
DM: We won't have to be constantly moving around and sharing our territory. Can you-
Delwath: You can't, you can't check whether there's still anything up in the tower for free, can you?
DM: No. But, but you're—you do—you counted exactly how many there were.
DM: And there's exactly that many.
Unknown: Yeah, that's what I was thinking. All right.
DM: So you give it to him?
Kenzo: Do I give it, do I give it now?
Wellby: No, when you, when you get there.
Delwath: No, because why when we get there? This is not to, this is not to get to the other tower. This is to get them all to not go fly off and tell the dragon.
Kenzo: As soon as I give it to him I kind of lose the leverage, don't I?
Delwath: Nah, 'cause he still wants to introduce us to his friend, right? Why does-
DM: It's up to you. It doesn't matter which way.

Kenzo: I'm gonna give it to you. I'll give it to you as soon as we get to your, the tower.

DM: ... it's only about a, it's like a mile and a half or two miles away.
Delwath: Right. Okay.

interactions.title: Walking and racing with Ghesh
lines: Kenzo: So just as, as we're, as we're walking, um, uh, his name is Ghesh again?

Kenzo: Uh, yeah, Kenzo's just like, you know, is just like shooting the shit with him. Just like, you know, it's like, "Tell me more about, like, so you got eight friends, you know? Is this, or is this your clan?"
Kenzo: "Is everybody related to you, or are you, you're... I mean, it seems like you're the boss here."

DM: Yeah, so you talk for a little bit. Like, the vibe you get is, like, I mean, there's, there's hundreds of, um, of these, of these, um... And he's, like, pretty, you know, he's pretty happy to talk to you now. He's like pretty-
Kenzo: Well, Kenzo's also genuinely just like, you know-
Kenzo: ... it's like, it's like he's, like, genuinely making some friends here.

DM: [coughs] There are, like, there's, you know, there's some that he—there's some of these dragonets that he kind of talks about as, like, the true believers that, you know, like Ra'ghemdros has like her little army, right? Like there's some people, there's some of them who are like very-
Delwath: The first person we're going to meet is a true believer.
DM: ... are just trying, you know, just trying to get by.
DM: It's kind of a boring place to live.
DM: They've been living here forever.
DM: The story is this is their homeland.
DM: Whether that's true or not, nobody knows.
DM: But, like, they claim this is where they've lived forever, and you know.

DM: Yeah. She, she's been here forever. We've been here forever. It's just the way it is.
Kenzo: And you've never seen any other people here, huh?

Kenzo: ... this plague dead thing over here, so there, 'cause there used to be humans here, right?
DM: Oh, yeah. A long, long time ago. They're all dead.
DM: Nobody, nobody really know, I mean...
Kenzo: So then you, you've got this one clan here. Are there, like, hundreds of clans here? How many clans are around here?
DM: Uh, there's, you know, dozens. Not hundreds. There's not that many of us.
DM: There's, you know, if you really wanna see something, you should, you should go see the games in the arena.
Kenzo: There are games in the arena?
Kenzo: Like, uh, like, you know, also games of luck or games of, uh-
DM: Oh, you couldn't play in these games.
DM: Um, you have to fly. Oh, you said you can fly. Let's race.
DM: Kenzo's like way, way faster than him, just totally crushes him.
Kenzo: He's... I thought you said that you could race.
DM: But Kenzo can only... You're using the raven whistle, right?
DM: So he flies up to you and he tries to smack the whistle out of your mouth. He's like, "You're cheating."

DM: Okay. Well, how long can you fly? Well, you can't talk while you're-
